messages:
Priya: quick question — for routing-policy changes exports, compliance wants full actor attribution but security wants minimal PII. how do we reconcile?
Matt: we need a pattern that works for both: NDJSON exports for regulators, but redacted views in console and public downloads.
Alex: agree. practically: include an `actor_ref` in the event stream and then optionally bundle a separate `actor_map` file that maps refs -> canonical identities for authorized consumers.
Sarah: +1. actor_map should be signed and only available if the export requester has the right scope (legal/subpoena or enterprise admin). otherwise show `actor_display: "[REDACTED]"` in UI/CSV.
John: quota question — generating actor_map for huge exports could be heavy. we should gate it behind an export type flag and limit by time range / size. also charge extra for signed mapping bundles.
Priya: makes sense. UX for rollouts: console should surface that a download contains sensitive mapping and require an extra confirmation step. link to policy in modal.
Matt: implementation sketch: events NDJSON shape with minimal actor token: 
```
{"ts":"2026-03-05T14:22:03Z","type":"policy.update","resource":"routing/policy/abc","change":"route->region:eu-west","actor_ref":"actor:U-12345"}
```
and an optional `actor_map.ndjson` with: 
```
{"actor_ref":"actor:U-12345","id":"U-12345","email":"alice@example.com","role":"platform-admin"}
```
Alex: we should hash stable identifiers in the public export (sha256) to avoid accidental PII leaks, e.g. `actor_ref: "hash:4f3b..."`. internal bundles keep plain refs.
Sarah: ok but hashing alone isn't access control. must combine hashing + signed bundle availability + audit trail. audit-bot: export-request by @Priya approved for tenant_acme, includes actor_map: false.
audit-bot: note: export package generated, size=12MB, id=exp-20260305-99.
Matt: API debate — do we expose a single endpoint `/exports` with query param `include_actor_map=true` or two endpoints `/exports` + `/actor-maps/{export_id}`?
John: prefer two endpoints. easier to enforce different auth scopes and throttles. actor-map endpoint can have elevated scope and separate quotas.
Priya: UX asks: show badge in exports list: "contains actor mapping" and require SSO reauth before download. mention in docs.
Alex: telemetry — add metric `export.actor_map.requested` and `export.actor_map.fetched` with tenant and principal tags. also surface in console security dashboard.
Sarah: retention: actor_map bundles should have short TTL (30d) and require explicit re-approval after TTL.
Matt: implementation tasks: 1) export NDJSON shape (Matt) 2) actor_map service + signing (Alex) 3) console badge + extra confirmation (Priya) 4) RBAC + quota per endpoint (John) 5) docs + example clients (Sarah).
Priya: timeline? want a small pilot for Dedicated customers in 3 weeks.
Matt: can do a minimal v1 in 3 weeks if we scope pilot to last-90-days and max 10k events.
John: I'll draft quota table and scopes this week.
Sarah: I'll write the privacy guideline and sample consent text for enterprise admins.
Priya: thanks all. created follow-up ticket: https://redwood.internal/boards/PLAT-1421 — please add estimates. :thumbsup:
Matt: noted.
Alex: one more: we need to ensure exports go through our redaction scanner before packaging. deferring until next sprint if heavy.
Priya: ok, capture that as optional risk item. closing for now.
